    Sasakian Manifolds

    Definitions

    There are many equivalent definitons of Sasakian manifold. We will take a viewpoint from Pseudo-Hermitian Geometry.

    Definition

    A Sasakian manifold is a pseudo-Hermitian manifold \((M,H,J,\theta)\), whose pseudo-Hermitian torsion \(\tau \) vanishes.

    The following proposition gives different characterizations of Sasakian manifolds.

    Proposition

    Let \((M^{2m+1},g)\) be a Riemannian manifold, \(\nabla\) the Levi-Civita connection, and \(R\) its curvature tensor. Then the following conditions are equivalent:

    1. \((M, g)\) is a Sasakian manifold.

    2. The associated cone manifold \((C(M), \tilde{g})= (M \times \rr^+,r^2g+dr^2)\) is a Kähler manifold. Therefore, Sasakian manifolds are the ``odd-dimensional'' generalization of Kähler manifolds.

    3. There exists a unit-length Killing vector field \(T\) on \(M\) such that the \((1,1)\)-type tensor field \(\Phi\) defined by \(\Phi(X) = \nabla_X T\) satisfies

      \[ (\nabla_X \Phi)(Y) = g(T, Y)X - g(X, Y)T , \quad \forall X,Y \in T(M). \]

    4. There exists a unit-length Killing vector field \(T\) on \(M\) such that the curvature satisfies

      \[ R(X, T)Y = g(T, Y)X - g(X, Y)T, \quad \forall X,Y \in T(M). \]

    5. There exists a unit-length Killing vector field \(T\) on \(M\) such that every section containing \(T\) has sectional curvature equal to \(1\).

    Remark

    Let \((M,g)\) be a Sasakian manifold and \(T\) the Killing vector field satisfying the above proposition. Then the tangent bundle admits the decomposition with respect to \(g\):

    \[ T(M)=H \otimes V_{T }. \]

    Define the \((1,1)\)-tensor field \(J_b=\Phi |_H\) on \(H\). Then by (iii) of the above proposition, it is easy to verify that \(J_b^2=-\id\). Note that the complex structure \(J_c\) on \((C(M),\tilde{g})\) is given by

    \[ J_c(Y)=\begin{cases} \Phi (Y)-g(T ,Y) r \frac{\partial }{\partial r} &\text{ if }~ Y \in T(M);\\ T &\text{ if }~ Y=r \frac{\partial }{\partial r}. \end{cases} \]

    Then, using the integrability of \(J_c\) and the fact that \(T\) is a Killing vector field, one can verify the formally integrable condition. Further analysis shows that \((M,H,J_b)\) is precisely the pseudo-Hermitian manifold with \(\tau=0\).
